findings.highlight: think back fondly on it in the following four months of our gray lives
findings.evidenceJa: 残る灰色だけの四か月に、思いを馳せざるを得なくなる
findings.explanation: With the festival over, the third-years are forced to turn their thoughts toward the four gray months that remain. The English instead has them spend those months reminiscing fondly about the festival, reversing the temporal direction and replacing dread of the future with nostalgia for the past.
findings.japanese:
学園生活最後の煌めきだった学園祭も終わり、
俺たち三年は、残る灰色だけの四か月に、
思いを馳せざるを得なくなる。
findings.todokanai: The school festival, the final bright event in our school life, has ended. All that we third-years can do now is to think back fondly on it in the following four months of our gray lives.

findings.highlight: the leftover number of students would be in the triple digits
findings.explanation: 三桁を切る means the remaining group falls below three digits—fewer than one hundred. The English says it remains in the triple digits, the opposite side of the stated threshold.
findings.japanese:
その中でも、他の大学に推薦の決まった強者や負け組、
就職を決めた社会人組を除くと、残るは三桁を切る。
findings.todokanai: This includes the ones who decided on other universities, be it because they're overachievers or underachievers, and the ones who have decided to go into employment. Take them away, and the leftover number of students would be in the triple digits.

findings.highlight: I see no reason for society to have to support another leech
findings.evidenceJa: 事情もない社会的弱者を生み出すつもりはないぞ
findings.explanation: Haruki says that, although Kazusa's family could support one NEET, he has no intention of creating a socially vulnerable person with no extenuating circumstances. The English invents society as her supporter and has Haruki call her a leech, making his intervention substantially more contemptuous and moralizing.
findings.japanese:
「確かにお前ん家の財力なら
ニートの一人くらい余裕だろうけど、俺はそんな、
事情もない社会的弱者を生み出すつもりはないぞ」
findings.todokanai: "With how rich your family is, you could probably get by just fine, even as a jobless NEET. Be that as it may, though, I see no reason for society to have to support another leech."

findings.explanation: Kazusa asks whether a hot-spring trip is suitable at their age. The English asks whether it is suitable in the present historical era, changing the object of her surprise.

findings.highlight: I don't exactly have any complaints
findings.evidenceJa: 問題がないわけじゃない
findings.explanation: Haruki concedes that the plan is not without problems. The English says he does not really have complaints, reversing the concession from acknowledged difficulties to near-approval.
findings.japanese: そりゃ、確かに問題がないわけじゃないけど…
findings.todokanai: Well, it's true that I don't exactly have any complaints…

findings.highlight: we're a couple that people wouldn't deem acceptable
findings.evidenceJa: 自他共に認める、認められないカップル
findings.explanation: Haruki's deliberate paradox is that they are, by their own and everyone else's admission, an 'unacceptable' or impossible-to-acknowledge couple. The English keeps only outsiders refusing approval and deletes the repeated 認める／認められない architecture and the couple's own recognition.
findings.japanese:
…俺たちは、自他共に認める、
認められないカップルなんだって。
findings.todokanai: I realize that we're a couple that people wouldn't deem acceptable.

findings.highlight: Since my subjects today were the same as hers
findings.evidenceJa: 昨日は、同じ教科だったから
findings.explanation: Haruki says yesterday's exam was in the same subject as Setsuna's, which at least let him study for himself while helping her. The English changes yesterday to today and singular subject to plural subjects.
findings.japanese:
昨日は、同じ教科だったから、
まだこっちも試験勉強できる分マシだった。
findings.todokanai: Since my subjects today were the same as hers, I figured I'd be able to get some studying in for myself as well.

findings.highlight: less than 30 minutes into the exam
findings.explanation: Haruki considers the answer-sheet switch once thirty minutes have already passed. The English places the thought before the thirty-minute point, reversing the explicit timing.
findings.japanese:
今日の試験も、もういっそのこと３０分過ぎた時点で
隣の席と答案用紙をすり替えるトリックを使おうかと
本気で悩んだ。
findings.todokanai: Even today, less than 30 minutes into the exam, I was seriously considering sneakily switching answer sheets with the person next to me.

findings.highlight: I'm going on a trip with someone
findings.explanation: Takeya's death-flag joke depends on Setsuna letting slip who she is traveling with—Haruki—so that he would decorate Haruki's desk with memorial flowers. The English quote discloses only that she is traveling with someone, removing the identifying information that would trigger the threat and making the punchline causally incoherent.
findings.japanese:
「…もしも『誰と旅行に行く』かを
彼女が誰かにポロリと漏らしたら、
お前の席に花だけは飾っておいてやるからな」
findings.todokanai: "If she carelessly spreads the news and blurts out, 'I'm going on a trip with someone,' I'll make sure to put some flowers on your desk, at the very least."

findings.highlight: Io's holding back from saying something
findings.evidenceJa: どこかやり切れなさみたいなものが見え隠れしてて
findings.explanation: Io's tone intermittently reveals helpless frustration or an unbearable, unresolved feeling. The English instead says she is withholding an unspoken message, replacing an emotional quality with a conversational intention.
findings.japanese:
そういうことよりも、依緒の口調には、
どこかやり切れなさみたいなものが見え隠れしてて、
なんだか、心がざわつく。
findings.todokanai: That aside, though, I can tell from her tone of voice that Io's holding back from saying something, and that's what really bothers me.
